title: GREENWOOD ARREST
full_story:
Pursuant to an investigation, on Tuesday, at approximately 9:27 am, officers with the Flora Police Department, with the assistance from Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip Givens, obtained and executed a search warrant in the 900 block of West 6th Street.

As a result of the search, Rodney J. Greenwood, 57, of Flora, was taken into custody on outstanding Clay County arrest warrants.  The warrants include charges of Grooming; Delivery of Controlled/Counterfeit Substance to a Person Under 18; Delivery of a Controlled Substance (Schedule III); Delivery of a Controlled Substance (Schedule IV); and two additional counts of Possession of a Controlled Substance.

Following his arrest, Greenwood was transported to the Flora Police Department for processing and later transferred to the custody of the Clay County Sheriff’s Office.

This investigation remains active, and additional charges may be forthcoming.

All individuals are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

title: WAYNE COUNTY ELECTION RESULTS
full_story:
Unofficial results from Tuesday’s Primary Election in Wayne County show that in the Republican race, for County Treasurer Yvette Anderson secured a decisive victory with 2,571 votes, defeating Celeste Garrett, who received 886 votes.  For County Clerk, Billie-Jo “BJ” Townsend narrowly defeated Janet Billington 1,785 votes to 1,734.  And for County Coroner Ryan Best won with 2,004 votes, Tom Windland received 915, and current Wayne County Coroner, Shari Winter garnered 634 votes.

title: SWCD SPRING TREE SALE
full_story:

title: FRIENDS OF THE LIBRARY SPRING BOOK SALE
full_story:

title: FISHING LICENSES EXPIRE
full_story:
As all 2025 Illinois fishing licenses expire on March 31st, new licenses for the 2026 season are now on sale.  Purchasing a fishing license grants access to Illinois’ lakes and rivers and directly supports conservation and outdoor education.

A standard, non-discounted resident fishing license costs just $15.  Licenses and stamps are available online and at local department-authorized vendors.

Those aged 16 and older are required to have a valid Illinois fishing license, with exemptions offered for those who are active-duty military personnel and for those with disabilities.

License and stamp sales also support the Illinois Department of Natural Resources’ (IDNR) Division of Fisheries, funding research, hatchery operations and invasive species prevention.

For regulations and a full list of license and stamp fees, visit ifishillinois.org.

title: DAY OF GIVING
full_story:
Illinois Eastern Community Colleges will host its first-ever Day of Giving on Tuesday, March 31st, inviting alumni, businesses and community members to support student success across its four campuses.

The 24-hour event will feature fundraising efforts led by the foundations of Frontier Community College, Lincoln Trail College, Olney Central College and Wabash Valley College. Each campus will focus on raising support for scholarships, programs and initiatives that benefit students.

IECC Vice Chancellor of Institutional Outreach Tona Ambrose said the idea for a coordinated Day of Giving grew out of the district’s recent reorganization and a renewed focus on strengthening alumni engagement.

“IECC has wanted to establish an alumni community for years, and with the collaborative reorganization of our district two years ago, it seemed like the perfect time to create our first Day of Giving,” Ambrose said.  “This event gives each of our college foundations an intentional opportunity to grow partnerships with alumni, businesses and community supporters who care deeply about student success.”

Since its founding in 1971, the Olney Central College Foundation has continually supported student and campus initiatives.

“We are really fortunate to have the Olney Central College Foundation to support all the different activities around campus,” said OCC President Chris Simpson.  “They are great partners, whether we’re looking at things to do in classrooms or working with faculty on providing financial support for innovative practices that they want to bring forward into their classrooms.”

OCC Foundation Executive Director Beth Miller said community support during events like the Day of Giving plays an important role in expanding opportunities for students.

“Community support is vital because Olney Central College serves the people and workforce of the region,” she said.  “When individuals and organizations give back, they are investing in local students and the future of the community.  That partnership helps the college continue expanding opportunities and preparing graduates to contribute to the local economy and community life.”

While scholarships remain a key focus, Miller said the foundation’s work encompasses so much more.

“While scholarships are a major focus, the Foundation also supports a wide range of initiatives that enhance the student experience,” she said.  “This includes funding for classroom equipment, program improvements, and campus projects that benefit students across many areas of study.  The Foundation’s support helps ensure students have the tools and opportunities they need to complete their education and reach their goals.”

Foundation support has helped fund scholarships, new technology, equipment and facility improvements that enhance the student experience.  Recently, the OCC Foundation played an essential role in the construction of the Health Professions Center, pledging more than $150,000 over five years to ensure the inclusion of a modern classroom space within the facility.  Donations toward the project totaled $125,660 last year.

In 2026, the OCC Foundation is supporting a planned $2 million project to renovate four science labs in Dr. Kent L. Wattleworth Hall.  The project will transform third-floor physics, chemistry and two biology labs into modern, high-tech learning spaces, with the foundation assisting through the purchase of state-of-the-art lab equipment.

“That project is getting underway this spring and will continue through the summer,” Simpson said.  “So not only are we going to be renovating those spaces but also upgrading much of the equipment and the materials and supplies the faculty are using and the students have access to.”

Community support remains essential to OCC’s ability to expand opportunities and enhance the educational experience for its students.

“It’s a really difficult time in higher education, particularly in community colleges with funding,” Simpson said.  “There are a number of shortfalls that we’re facing and without having outside support, then I think we would be unable to meet some of the needs of our students and be able to provide them exactly what it is they’re looking for with their post-secondary experience.”

Because of those challenges, Simpson said fundraising efforts such as the Day of Giving, and the Foundation’s annual Campaign for Excellence are essential.

“I hope they recognize that they are directly impacting the educational experience of a student,” Simpson said of donors.  “If you are giving, then know that that money is going to directly impact the students’ experience while they’re attending Olney Central College.”

Simpson also expressed appreciation for the donors and community members who continue to support OCC.

“One of the things that I’ve noticed in the time that I’ve been president is how generous our community is,” he said.  “They support Olney Central College.  We wouldn’t be able to do it without them.”

To participate in OCC’s Day of Giving, visit www.iecc.edu/occ-day-giving.

title: JD POWERS RANKING
full_story:
Edward Jones, a leading financial services firm, reclaimed the No. 1 spot among 23 advice-based firms in the JD Power 2026 US Investor Satisfaction Study(SM), marking the first time the firm has earned the top rank since 2021.  This achievement reflects meaningful progress in Edward Jones’ journey to deliver comprehensive advice and planning and expanded products and services to serve more clients, more completely.

Edward Jones achieved Best-in-Class performance in four of the seven most influential dimensions of investor satisfaction, including trust, people, products meeting client needs and ease of doing business, all while continuing to enhance its digital capabilities and value for fees paid.  The firm earned an Overall Satisfaction score of 754 on a 1,000-point scale, one of only three firms scoring significantly above the advised-industry average of 725.  The results underscore the strength of Edward Jones’ relationship-based model and the trust clients place in the firm in an increasingly competitive landscape.

The firm’s financial advisors take a personalized, relationship-driven approach by partnering with clients to learn about their goals, priorities and life circumstances before developing tailored financial strategies.  Supported by the firm’s financial planning capabilities, investment solutions and digital tools, this model is designed to deliver advice that evolves with clients over time and helps them stay focused on achieving their long-term financial goals.

In recent years, the firm has invested in advanced technology, financial advisor education and a range of new product offerings to help improve the financial advisor experience and better meet clients’ needs.  This includes integrated banking capabilities, expanded private-client wealth services and alternative investments, and new portfolio-management technology to support personalized managed accounts.  The firm also launched Edward Jones Ventures to invest in and incubate innovations that can enhance financial planning, advisor capabilities and client experiences.

The study evaluates the experiences of investors working with a wealth management firm, in either an advised or DIY capacity in seven dimensions (in alphabetical order): digital channels; ease of doing business; people; product and service offerings; resolving problems or complaints; trust; and value for fees paid.

The JD Power 2026 US Investor Satisfaction Study(SM) was fielded from January 2025 through January 2026 and is based on responses from 7,982 advised and 4,335 DIY investors.  For more information, visit jdpower.com/awards.

title: TURKEY FEDERATION SCHOLARSHIP
full_story:
The Illinois State Chapter of the National Wild Turkey Federation is now accepting scholarship applications.  Applicants must be Illinois residents enrolled in a public community college, public four-year college, or public university in Illinois.  Eligible majors include conservation, wildlife management, ecology, conservation law enforcement, wildlife medicine, or related fields approved by the committee.

For details and how to apply, visit ilnwtf.org and click on “Scholarships.”  Application must be postmarked by Saturday, May 1, 2026

title: DOT ROUTE 66 MAP
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation announced the release of a  new Illinois Route 66 Map in honor of the iconic road’s 100th birthday this year.  The map takes a nostalgic look at America’s most famous highway and sights to see in Illinois, while providing a historical timeline of the route’s evolution and its cultural impact.

“The new Route 66 map is a must for enthusiasts and road trippers celebrating the 100th anniversary of the Mother Road,” said Illinois Transportation Secretary Gia Biagi.  “You can get your kicks with a detailed overview of the highway that’s the best as it stretches across Illinois, highlighting towns large and small that are perfect for pit stops and Route 66’s legendary roadside attractions.”

With the centennial expected to unite preservationists, tourism leaders and enthusiasts from around the world, the map will provide a touchpoint in Illinois to help celebrate the past, with a look toward the next century of adventure on Route 66.

The map was developed in collaboration with the Illinois Route 66 Scenic Byway.

“The last Illinois Route 66 paper map was created in 1998, so it’s incredibly exciting to see a new version celebrating the Mother Road,” said Illinois Route 66 Scenic Byway Executive Director Casey Claypool.  “Route 66 has always been about Americana, nostalgia and the joy of the journey, so having something fresh that travelers can hold in their hands will spark curiosity and inspire road trips.  We’re deeply grateful for the continued support from IDOT.”

The Illinois Route 66 Map is paid with funds from the Federal Highway Administration and published by IDOT on recycled paper.  The map is printed with vegetable-based inks.

To request a map, complete the form at https://idot.click/map-request or email [email protected].  Free copies also will be available at interstate rest areas.
